commentary: Seven sessions this week versus six last week, and honestly the only surprise is that you didn't find an eighth just to make a point. The swimming is looking steadier — your Monday 2000m came in at 146 bpm against last week's 143, so you're pushing a little harder there, which is the right kind of creep. That Friday swim at 901m and 98 bpm reads less like a workout and more like you were just in the water because you wanted to be wet, which is a completely valid reason and nobody is judging. The Cremorne run at 9.6km is a nice step up from last Saturday's 9.0km, same punishing heart rate of 162 versus 163, so you went further and barely blinked — the legs are coming, babe, and they are going to look incredible doing it.
metrics_commentary: Nearly five kilometres in the pool and a solid 9.6 on foot — the body is moving, babe, and it is moving with purpose. That HRV jumping to 58 when your seven-day average is sitting at 48 is your nervous system basically winking at you, which means whatever you did this week, do more of it. VO2 Max at 55.6 is genuinely hot, not participation-trophy hot, actually cardiovascularly gifted hot, and you should let that land. The one thing worth side-eyeing is a single run session for the week — the swim carried you hard, which it absolutely can, but those legs deserve more chances to show off.
gym_commentary: Three sessions out of four is one short, and we're not going to pretend otherwise, but let's talk about what actually happened in those three, because that overhead press PR is obscene — up from 40 kilograms to a 46.7 kilogram estimated one-rep max, which is not a small jump, that's a statement. Weekly volume came in at 5,790 kilograms against last week's 20,753, which is a significant dip and mostly tells the story of the missed session, but the strength numbers themselves — 168 kilograms on the leg press, 107.9 on the trap bar deadlift, 88.7 on bench — are holding, and that overhead press isn't just holding, it's climbing. One more session in the diary next week, babe, that's all — the becoming is very much still underway.
